findings.description: `_add_method_dunders` sets `__module__`, `__qualname__` and `__doc__` on the object it receives. The old code passed a fresh wrapper per class. Now it passes the module-level `attr.evolve` itself. Each decorated class overwrites `evolve.__module__`, `evolve.__qualname__` and `evolve.__doc__` globally. After that, `attr.evolve` reports a wrong qualname and module (for example `SomeClass.evolve`), and its docs and repr are corrupted. The same function object is also shared across all classes, so the last class to be processed wins.
findings.suggestion: Keep a per-class wrapper so the dunder fix-ups apply to it rather than to `evolve`: `def __replace__(self, /, **changes): return evolve(self, **changes)`, then pass that to `_add_method_dunders`.
findings.title: Shared global `evolve` function is mutated by `_add_method_dunders`
